questions.text: Which Stone Age period came first — Mesolithic, Neolithic or Paleolithic?
questions.funfact: The Paleolithic (Old Stone Age) began around 3.3 million years ago, followed by the Mesolithic around 10,000 BC and the Neolithic around 4,000 BC.

questions.funfact: 🦵 The kneecap (patella) is the largest sesamoid bone in the human body — and babies aren't born with one. It develops between ages 2 and 6.

questions.text: How many years of marriage does a silver anniversary signify?
questions.funfact: 💍 The tradition of anniversary gifts by year dates back to medieval Germany. The golden anniversary (50 years) was the first to be widely celebrated.

questions.text: Is mortadella a type of cured meat, cream cheese or dessert wine?
questions.funfact: 🥩 Mortadella originated in Bologna, Italy, which is exactly why Americans started calling cheap processed luncheon meat 'bologna' (or 'baloney').

questions.text: Which club won the 2026 UEFA Champions League final, defending their title from the previous season?
questions.funfact: ⚽ PSG became only the second club in Champions League era history to defend the title, matching Real Madrid's back-to-back wins in 2016 and 2017.

questions.text: In what year was Star Wars released for the first time, did Elvis Presley die at Graceland, and did the first Apple II computer go on sale?
Which animal is the official mascot of Coca-Cola?
questions.funfact: 🐻‍❄️ The Coca-Cola polar bear first appeared in a French advert in 1922, but didn't become the animated icon we know today until the 1993 'Northern Lights' TV commercial.

questions.text: Which garnish is traditionally used in a dirty martini?
questions.funfact: 🍸 A martini becomes 'dirty' when olive brine is added to the mix. If you ask for it 'filthy', even more brine goes in. The olive garnish is said to have been added by President FDR.

questions.text: How many strings does a standard ukulele have?
questions.funfact: 🎸 The ukulele was brought to Hawaii in 1879 by Portuguese immigrants from Madeira. Its name roughly translates as 'jumping flea' in Hawaiian.

questions.text: Which is the only bird that can fly backwards?
questions.funfact: 🐦 Hummingbirds beat their wings up to 80 times per second and are the only birds that can hover in mid-air, fly sideways, and even upside down as well as backwards.

questions.text: Name the 5 highest-grossing English-language animated sequel movies with the number 2 or II in the title (1 point each)
According to the tongue twister, what did Peter Piper pick a peck of? (Hint: 2 words)
questions.funfact: 🌶️ A 'peck' is an actual unit of measurement, roughly 9 litres. So Peter Piper picked a very large quantity of pickled peppers.

questions.text: Who was the lead singer of The Supremes during the 1960s?
Which car manufacturer owns brands including Audi, Porsche, Škoda, Lamborghini and Ducati?
questions.funfact: 🚗 Volkswagen means 'people's car' in German. The company was originally founded in 1937 with the goal of producing an affordable car for ordinary German workers.

questions.text: Complete the next five words in Cher’s Believe: Do you believe in life after love? I can feel something inside me say I really _____ _____ _____ _____ _____
questions.funfact: 🎵 Believe was the first major pop song to use Auto-Tune as a deliberate effect. Cher's team were so protective of the technique they initially claimed it was a 'vocoder' to keep it secret.

questions.text: Who was born first — Oprah Winfrey or Madonna?
questions.funfact: 📅 Oprah was born on 29 January 1954, Madonna on 16 August 1958, making Oprah four and a half years older.

questions.text: Which U.S. state was the 50th and final state to join the union, in 1959?
questions.funfact: 🌺 Hawaii is the only US state made up entirely of islands, the only one located in Oceania, and the only one to grow coffee commercially.

questions.text: What is the name of the host of the YouTube series Hot Ones?
questions.funfact: 🌶️ Sean Evans has hosted over 360 episodes and estimates he's eaten more than 3,000 hot wings. The show has amassed over 4 billion views on YouTube.

questions.text: The name of which Indonesian island is an anagram of an item of cricket equipment?
questions.funfact: 🏏 A cricket bail, the small piece of wood balanced on top of the stumps

questions.text: Which EGOT winner claimed their Emmy for 'Beyond Tara' and also 'The View', their Grammy for a Broadway comedy recording, their Oscar for Best Supporting Actress in the movie 'Ghost', and their Tony for producing 'Thoroughly Modern Millie'?
questions.shoutout: 🙌 Big shoutout to Lucas for this question!
questions.funfact: 🏆 Whoopi completed her EGOT in 2002, becoming the first Black woman and first Black performer to achieve it. Only around 20 people in history have ever won all four major entertainment awards.

questions.text: The day before yesterday I was 25, next year I will be 28. What day is my birthday? (Format example: 12 September)
questions.funfact: 🎂 The logic: if today is 1 January, the day before yesterday was 30 December — when you were still 25. You turned 26 on 31 December, and will turn 27 later this year, then 28 next year.

questions.text: 'Oh... and it is LOVELY! You know, you're really quite a decorator. It's amazing what you've done with such a modest budget. I like that boulder. That is a NICE boulder.' — which movie is this quote from?
questions.funfact: Shrek was the first ever film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature when the category was introduced in 2002.

questions.text: Who won the 2026 Roland Garros men's singles title?
questions.funfact: 🎾 Zverevs first Grand Slam Title.

questions.text: The Spanish phrase 'hasta la vista' translates to what in English?
questions.funfact: 🤖 Arnold Schwarzenegger's delivery of 'hasta la vista, baby' in Terminator 2 made it one of cinema's most quoted lines — but in the Spanish-dubbed version of the film, the line was changed to 'sayonara, baby' instead.

questions.text: How many teams are competing in the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.funfact: ⚽ The 2026 World Cup is the first to feature 48 teams, up from 32 — meaning 104 matches will be played across the USA, Canada and Mexico, making it the biggest World Cup in history.

questions.text: Which scientist is an anagram of RADIUM CAMEE
questions.funfact: ⚗️ Marie Curie is the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911. She remains the only woman to have won two Nobel Prizes.

questions.text: Baba ganoush is primarily made from which ingredient?
questions.funfact: 🍆 The name 'baba ganoush' is thought to come from Arabic meaning 'pampered daddy' — a playful name for a dish supposedly made to please a toothless elder who couldn't chew.

questions.text: Which performer was born Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta?
questions.funfact: 🎤 Lady Gaga's stage name was inspired by the Queen song 'Radio Ga Ga.' Her producer texted her 'Lady Gaga' as a nickname and she loved it so much she never looked back.

questions.text: Which of these companies is NOT owned by Microsoft?
questions.funfact: 🎵 Microsoft paid $26 billion for LinkedIn in 2016 — its largest ever acquisition at the time.

questions.text: Which of these colours appears on the most national flags in the world?
questions.funfact: 🚩 Red is actually the single most common colour on all flags worldwide, but of these four options yellow/gold wins — appearing on roughly 46% of all national flags, often symbolising wealth, the sun or natural resources.

questions.text: In what year did Call Me Maybe get released in Canada, did the TV show Suits first air, and did a 9.1 magnitude earthquake hit Japan?
questions.funfact: 🎵 Call Me Maybe was originally only a modest Canadian hit until Justin Bieber tweeted about it in early 2012 — within weeks it became one of the best-selling singles of all time.

questions.text: What does the C in SCUBA stand for?
questions.funfact: 🤿 Self Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus. The word 'scuba' was coined in 1952 by US Army Major Christian Lambertsen, who also invented an early version of the device during World War II for use by Navy frogmen on covert underwater missions.

questions.text: If someone was described as 'hard boiled' in old-fashioned slang, what does it mean?
questions.funfact: 🕵️ 'Hard boiled' became popular in 1920s America to describe no-nonsense detectives in pulp fiction novels. Raymond Chandler and Dashiell Hammett made the term iconic through characters like Philip Marlowe and Sam Spade.

questions.text: Which American company has the most employees in the world?
questions.funfact: 🛒 Walmart has 2.1 million employees globally. If its workforce were a country it would be the 148th most populous nation on earth — bigger than Slovenia, Qatar and Bahrain combined.

questions.text: What does HBO stand for, the American TV Network?
questions.funfact: 📺 HBO launched in 1972 and was the first TV channel to broadcast via satellite in 1975 — the first event they aired was the legendary 'Thrilla in Manila' between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier.

questions.text: Brazil has won the most FIFA World Cups with 5 titles. Name the other 5 countries that have won 2 or more (1 point each)
questions.funfact: 🏆 Brazil is the only nation to have appeared in every single FIFA World Cup — all 23 editions — and remain the record holders with 5 titles. The other winners: Germany (4), Italy (4), Argentina (3), France (2) and Uruguay (2).

questions.text: Which artist announced their 8th studio album 'Petal' with the lead single 'Hate That I Made You Love Me'?
questions.funfact: 🎵 'Hate That I Made You Love Me' debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — the first single from each of Grande's eight albums has debuted in the top 10, with the last four all hitting No. 1 straight away.

questions.text: Complete the next five words: 'Buying bread from a man in Brussels / He was six-foot-four and full of muscles / I said do you speak-a my language / He just smiled and —' (Hint: contains an Australian condiment)
questions.funfact: 🥪 'Down Under' by Men at Work (1981) is arguably Australia's most famous song — but the band were sued in 2010 over the flute riff allegedly copying a 1934 children's folk song 'Kookaburra Sits in the Old Gum Tree'.

questions.text: Which animal has the highest blood pressure of any creature on earth?
questions.funfact: 🦒 A giraffe's blood pressure is roughly double that of a human — it needs such high pressure to pump blood all the way up its 1.8-metre neck to reach its brain. Its heart alone weighs around 11kg.

questions.text: In the Google logo, what colour is the second letter O?
questions.funfact: 🎨 The Google logo uses only primary colours — except for the second L in the old logo, which is green, a secondary colour. This was intentional to show that Google 'doesn't follow the rules'.

questions.text: Which country drinks more Guinness — Ireland or Nigeria?
questions.funfact: 🍺 Nigeria has been the world's second-largest Guinness market since 2007, behind only Great Britain. Nigerian Guinness is also almost twice as strong — 7.5% ABV vs 4.2% — and is brewed with locally grown maize and sorghum.

questions.text: Which of these celebrities had the biggest age gap between themselves and their youngest child?
questions.funfact: 👶 Al Pacino was 83, De Niro was 79, Mick Jagger was 73 and Rod Stewart was 66. Remarkably, De Niro and Pacino — who played father and son in The Godfather Part II — both had babies within weeks of each other in 2023.

questions.text: What word can go BEFORE 'tone' and 'bearer', and AFTER 'ear'?
questions.funfact: 💍 The tradition of wearing a wedding ring on the fourth finger of the left hand dates back to ancient Rome, where it was believed a vein ran directly from that finger to the heart — called the 'Vena Amoris' or Vein of Love.

questions.text: Which part of the brain is primarily responsible for regulating your breathing?
questions.funfact: 🧠 The medulla oblongata controls breathing, heart rate and blood pressure. The cerebellum controls balance and coordination. The hippocampus handles memory and navigation. The amygdala processes emotions like fear and pleasure.

questions.text: If you are looking forward at the front of a boat, what is the right side of the vessel called?
questions.shoutout: 🙌 Big shoutout to Dad for this question!
questions.funfact: ⛵ 'Starboard' comes from Old English meaning the steering side — early boats were steered with an oar on the right. The left side 'port' gets its name because sailors docked on that side to avoid damaging the steering oar.

questions.text: Puzzle Question: A travel agent receives 54 bookings for Lanzarote, 22 for Bali, 34 for Jamaica and 43 for Florida. How many bookings do they take for Ibiza?
questions.funfact: 🧮 The trick: the first digit = number of consonants, the second digit = number of vowels. Ibiza has 2 consonants (b, z) and 3 vowels (I, i, a) = 23.

questions.text: 'I wish I knew how to quit you' — which movie is this iconic line from?
questions.funfact: 🤠 Brokeback Mountain (2005) won 3 Academy Awards including Best Director for Ang Lee, but lost Best Picture to Crash in one of the most controversial Oscar upsets in history.

questions.text: What do you call a group of lions?
questions.funfact: 🦁 A pride of lions usually consists of around 15 lions — mostly related females and their cubs, with a small number of resident males.

questions.text: The 'Cosmo' cocktail is short for what?
questions.funfact: 🍸 The Cosmopolitan rose to global fame thanks to Sex and the City, where Carrie Bradshaw and friends drank them throughout the series — sparking a worldwide cocktail trend in the late 1990s and 2000s.

questions.text: Which 2026 Pride event is estimated to draw the largest attendance often cited in the millions?
questions.funfact: 🌈 São Paulo Pride regularly draws crowds estimated between 3-5 million people, making it the largest Pride celebration in the World far surpassing NYC Pride's 2 million+ turnout.

questions.text: Unscramble this Music Icon: A DAMN NO
questions.funfact: 🎤 Madonna has long been celebrated as one of the music industry's most outspoken LGBTQ+ allies, dedicating her 1989 song 'Vogue' to the New York ballroom scene and headlining countless Pride events throughout her career.

questions.text: What shape of clear block can you use to help make a rainbow on a wall indoors?
questions.funfact: 🌈 A prism splits white light into the colours of the rainbow through a process called dispersion — different wavelengths of light bend at slightly different angles as they pass through the glass.

questions.text: Who hosts Drag Race?
questions.funfact: 👑 RuPaul has won an Emmy for Outstanding Host for a Reality or Competition Program a record-breaking number of times, and is the most decorated Black entertainer in Emmy history.

questions.text: Alan Turing is one of the most notable LGBTQ+ scientists from history. Which German code did his machine, the Bombe, help to break?
questions.funfact: 💻 Turing's Bombe machine is estimated to have shortened World War II by 2-4 years, saving millions of lives. Tragically, Turing was later persecuted for his homosexuality and died in 1954 — he received a posthumous royal pardon in 2013.

questions.text: In which city did the Rainbow Pride flag originate in 1978?
questions.funfact: 🏳️‍🌈 The flag was created by artist Gilbert Baker for San Francisco's Gay Freedom Day parade. The original flag had 8 colours, but two were dropped due to fabric availability, leaving the now-iconic 6-stripe design.

questions.text: In what year was Call Me By Your Name released, did Dua Lipa release 'New Rules', and did Australia legalise same-sex marriage? (Year Format: YYYY)
questions.funfact: 🏳️‍🌈 Australia's same-sex marriage law passed with overwhelming public support — a national postal survey showed 61.6% in favour before parliament voted to legalise it in December 2017.

questions.text: In the song and organisation YMCA, what does the C stand for?
questions.funfact: 🏳️‍🌈 YMCA stands for Young Men's Christian Association, founded in London in 1844. The Village People's 1978 song of the same name has since become an enduring gay anthem, despite the band always denying any explicit LGBTQ+ meaning.

questions.text: In Gen Z slang, what does 'slay' mean?
options: To excel or succeed with style and confidence
questions.funfact: 💅 'Slay' has roots in Black and ballroom culture dating back decades before going mainstream — ballroom culture, pioneered by LGBTQ+ communities of colour in the 1980s, has heavily influenced modern internet slang.

questions.text: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for owning which breed of dog?
questions.funfact: 🐕 The Queen owned over 30 corgis during her reign, all descended from her first corgi Susan, gifted to her on her 18th birthday in 1944.

questions.text: Who wrote 'The Picture of Dorian Gray'?
questions.funfact: 📖 Oscar Wilde was later imprisoned for 'gross indecency' due to his relationships with men — a conviction that destroyed his career and health. He was given a posthumous pardon by the UK government in 2017.

questions.text: Name ABBA's top 5 most streamed songs on Spotify (1 point each)
answers: lay all your love on me
acceptedAnswers: lay all your love on me
questions.funfact: 💃 Dancing Queen is ABBA's most streamed song with over 2 billion streams — it was written specifically to be performed at the wedding of King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden in 1976.

questions.text: 'I Will Survive' wins the first and last Grammy ever awarded for Best Disco Recording. Who was the artist?
questions.funfact: 🪩 The Best Disco Recording category was created and retired in the same year — 1980 — after backlash against disco's mainstream dominance. Gaynor's hit has since become a global gay-rights anthem covered in over 20 languages.

questions.text: Complete the next five words: 'I'm never gonna dance again, guilty feet have got no rhythm, though it's easy to pretend, I —'
questions.funfact: 🎶 This is from 'Careless Whisper' by George Michael — co-written when he was just 17, it became one of the best-selling singles of all time, with over 6 million UK certified sales alone.

questions.text: What movie did Tom Hanks win his first Best Actor Oscar for, playing a gay lawyer with AIDS?
questions.funfact: Many of the courtroom extras were real people living with HIV/AIDS, recruited through the Philadelphia support group ActionAIDS.

questions.text: What does 'Mardi Gras' mean in French?
questions.funfact: 🎭 Mardi Gras gets its name because it's the last day to indulge in rich, fatty foods before the fasting period of Lent begins on Ash Wednesday.

questions.text: Who has more US Billboard Hot 100 #1 hits — Elton John or Queen?
questions.funfact: 🎹 Elton John has 9 US #1 hits including 'Candle in the Wind 1997' and 'That's What Friends Are For'. Queen only managed 2 — 'Crazy Little Thing Called Love' and 'Another One Bites the Dust'. Surprisingly, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' never hit #1 in the US, peaking at #2.

questions.text: What dance was performed in 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show'?
questions.funfact: 🎬 The term 'Easter Egg' is said to have originated from this movie — the cast supposedly left actual Easter eggs lying around on set, and spotting them in the finished film became a fun tradition for fans.

questions.text: What word can fill in the blank: '_s of the Stone Age', '_ of Hearts' and 'Priscilla, _ of the Desert'?
questions.funfact: 🎬 'The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert' (1994) became a landmark LGBTQ+ film, later adapted into a hit stage musical that has toured the world.

questions.text: Which famous fashion designer has also directed Oscar-nominated movies such as 'Nocturnal Animals' and 'A Single Man'?
questions.funfact: 🎬 Before becoming a director, Tom Ford spent a decade as creative director of Gucci and Yves Saint Laurent.

questions.text: The first openly gay prime minister, Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir, hailed from which country?
questions.shoutout: 🙌 Big shoutout to Talisia for this question!
questions.funfact: 🇮🇸 Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir served as Iceland's Prime Minister from 2009 to 2013, becoming the world's first openly lesbian head of government in modern history.

questions.text: In old Nokia phone keypad language (T9 texting), what does the following translate as: 44 2 7 7 999 0 7 777 444 3 33?
questions.funfact: 📱 Old Nokia phones used T9 predictive text where each number key represented 3-4 letters texting fluently on these keypads was practically a rite of passage for anyone who grew up in the 2000s!

weekly_quizzes.title: Big Fat Sunday Quiz #11
weekly_quizzes.description: Bens Trivia is proudly partnering up with Windsor Bowls Club in Brisbane Australia, the very first venue to get Bens Trivia Coasters! 🙌 Big Shoutout to Windsor Bowls Club!

questions.text: Which film has the opening line - The key to faking out the parents is the clammy hands. It's a good non-specific symptom; I'm a big believer in it
questions.funfact: The line is from Ferris Bueller's Day Off (1986), the script was famously written by John Hughes in just six days.

questions.text: Which player has just broken the all-time record for most goals scored at FIFA World Cups?
questions.funfact: Messi broke Miroslav Klose's long-standing record of 16 goals during the 2026 World Cup, becoming the tournament's all-time top scorer.

questions.text: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, which word represents the letter Q?
questions.funfact: Quebec is also the only NATO phonetic alphabet word named after a place rather than a generic word.

questions.text: Which country will host both the 2027 Rugby World Cup and the 2032 Olympics?
questions.funfact: Brisbane will specifically host the 2032 Olympics, while the Rugby World Cup matches will be spread across multiple Australian cities.

questions.text: Which actress is an anagram of TRY EEL SPERM"?
questions.funfact: Meryl Streep holds the record for the most acting Oscar nominations (21) and has won three times.

questions.text: Sumo wrestling has deep ceremonial ties to which religion?
questions.funfact: Many sumo rituals, like the purification of the ring with salt, come directly from Shinto practices.

questions.text: Caitlyn Jenner (formerly known as Bruce Jenner) won Olympic gold in 1976. Which event did she compete in?
questions.funfact: Jenner set a world record of 8,618 points winning the decathlon at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, earning the unofficial title of 'world's greatest athlete'.

questions.text: Which letter of the alphabet do the most chemical elements begin with?
questions.funfact: 12 elements start with C — including Carbon, Calcium, Chromium, Copper, Caesium, and Curium — more than any other letter.

questions.text: The surname Kim is most commonly found in which country?
questions.funfact: About 1 in 5 South Koreans and 1 in 4 North Koreans are named Kim, making it one of the most concentrated surnames in the world.

questions.text: In which year did Princess Diana die, the Spice Girls release 'Wannabe', and Good Will Hunting come out?
questions.funfact: Princess Diana's death in August 1997 became one of the most-watched news events in history.

questions.text: In corporate/business language, what does the acronym ICT stand for?
questions.funfact: ICT is often used instead of just 'IT' to emphasise the role of communications (like networks and telecoms) alongside computing.

questions.text: Finish the saying: "It's better to light a candle than to curse the..."
questions.funfact: While often misattributed to ancient Chinese philosophy or Eleanor Roosevelt, the phrase was actually coined by English Methodist preacher William Lonsdale Watkinson in a 1907 sermon.

questions.text: Which country is widely ranked as having the fastest average internet speed in the world?
questions.funfact: Singapore has topped global broadband speed rankings for several years running, thanks to its dense fibre infrastructure.

questions.text: Which of these happened first?
questions.funfact: Captain Cook reached Australia's east coast in 1770, the US declared independence in 1776, the French Revolution began in 1789, and the Irish Famine started in 1845.

questions.text: 2 of the 7 Wonders of the (Modern) World are Petra and Chichen Itza. Name the other 5 (hint: their countries start with C, B, P, I, and I).
questions.funfact: These are the New7Wonders of the World, chosen by a global public poll in 2007. The Great Pyramid of Giza, the only surviving wonder of the ancient world, wasn't part of the vote but was given honorary 8th-wonder status.

questions.text: What was the title of Adele's first studio album? (Hint: A number)
questions.funfact: Released in 2008, 19 was named for Adele's age while writing most of its songs, a naming convention she repeated with 21, 25, and 30.

questions.text: I don't wanna close my eyes, I don't wanna fall asleep, 'Cause I'd miss you baby, And I don't wanna miss a thing, 'Cause even when I dream of you, The _
questions.funfact: It was Aerosmith's only number-one single on the Billboard Hot 100, and was written by Diane Warren specifically for the film Armageddon.

questions.text: Besides the 4 species of echidna, there's only one other mammal that lays eggs. What is it?
questions.funfact: Echidnas and platypuses together make up the monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young.

questions.text: What is the name of the man on the KFC logo?
questions.funfact: Sanders made surprise visits to KFC restaurants and frequently complained to the press about the food quality. He famously called their newly formulated gravy 'wallpaper paste' and 'sludge'.

questions.text: Which is taller: the Eiffel Tower or the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
questions.funfact: The Eiffel Tower stands about 330 metres tall, while the Leaning Tower of Pisa is only around 56 metres, the Eiffel Tower is roughly six times taller.

questions.text: Why was the world's first webcam created, back in 1991?
options: To monitor a server room's temperature
To check if a coffee pot was full
For a university's CCTV security system
questions.funfact: Researchers at Cambridge University's Computer Lab set up a camera pointed at their coffee pot so they wouldn't waste a trip to find it empty.

questions.text: What single word can go before 'hold', before 'rail', and after 'before'?
questions.funfact: That gives you 'handhold', 'handrail', and 'beforehand'.

questions.text: Nickelback, Voting, and Silverback all share a common link. Which of these words can also be included?
questions.funfact: All of these words contain an element from the pariodic table. Bandleader hides (lead) joining nickelback (nickel), voting (tin), and silverback (silver) as another word with a chemical element hidden inside.

questions.text: Dave Dobbyn's 'Slice of Heaven' (with Herbs) was written for which 1986 New Zealand film?
questions.shoutout: 🙌 Shoutout to Danielle for this one!
questions.funfact: The song went on to spend 8 weeks at number one in New Zealand. It was often used in TV ads to encourage people to visit New Zealand.

questions.text: How many possible opening moves does White have on the very first move of a chess game?
questions.funfact: Each of White's 8 pawns can move 1 or 2 squares (16 options), plus each of the 2 knights has 2 possible moves (4 options) giving 20 total.

questions.text: Which film features the line - You had me at hello?,

text.text: What animal year is 2026 according to the Chinese zodiac calendar?
text.funfact: 2026 is specifically the Year of the Fire Horse, beginning 17 February 2026 and ending 5 February 2027.

text.text: What is "goodbye" in Italian?
text.funfact: Ciao is actually used for both 'hello' and 'goodbye' in informal Italian, while 'Arrivederci' is the more formal farewell.

text.text: On what date does France celebrate Bastille Day?
text.funfact: Bastille Day marks the storming of the Bastille prison on 14 July 1789, a key event of the French Revolution.

text.text: Which singer is an anagram of VERILY SLEEPS?
text.funfact: Elvis Presley is often called 'The King of Rock and Roll' and remains one of the best-selling solo artists in history.

text.text: What is the traditional garnish for an Old Fashioned cocktail?
text.funfact: A maraschino cherry is sometimes added too, but the orange peel (twisted to release its oils) is considered the classic garnish.

text.text: What colour is most associated with the company Tiffany & Co.?
text.funfact: Tiffany Blue has been a registered trademark colour since 1998 and is officially known as Pantone 1837, named after Tiffany's founding year.

text.text: Which is the most lethal?
text.funfact: Apple seeds contain amygdalin, a natural compound of cyanide and sugar. You would have to meticulously chew and crush anywhere from 150 to several thousand seeds in one sitting to be at risk.

text.text: Which is the only country in the world whose name ends with the letter H?
text.funfact: Bangladesh is the only country whose English name ends in 'h'.

text.text: In which year did Martin Luther King Jr. deliver his 'I Have a Dream' speech, JFK get assassinated, and The Beatles release their first album 'Please Please Me'?
text.funfact: All three events happened within months of each other in 1963, a hugely consequential year in world history.

text.text: What does the acronym GMT stand for?
text.funfact: GMT is based on the mean solar time at the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, and was historically used as the basis for world time zones.

text.text: Finish the phrase: 'Lions for...'
text.funfact: The phrase 'lions led by donkeys' is a related but different saying about WWI soldiers being poorly commanded; 'Lions for Lambs' is also the title of a 2007 film starring Tom Cruise and Robert Redford.

text.text: What is the name for fermented honey, often considered one of the oldest alcoholic drinks in the world?
text.funfact: Mead is made by fermenting honey with water and is sometimes called 'honey wine', despite not using grapes.

text.text: Which of these gods came first?
text.funfact: Ra was worshipped in ancient Egypt from at least 2600 BCE, long before Buddha (c. 5th century BCE), Jesus (c. 4 BCE–30 CE), or Muhammad (c. 570–632 CE).

text.text: Name the top 5 countries by tea consumption per capita.
text.funfact: Turkey tops global per-capita tea consumption, with the average Turk drinking several cups a day.

text.text: Who originally wrote and sang 'Make You Feel My Love', later made famous by Adele?
text.funfact: Dylan wrote it for his 1997 album Time Out of Mind. Billy Joel actually released his own cover first, two months before Dylan's version came out, but Dylan wrote the song.

text.text: What are the next 5 lyrics - Sweet Dreams Are Made of these_
text.funfact: The song, by Eurythmics, was released in 1983 and became one of the most recognisable synth-pop tracks of the decade.

text.text: Hippos famously secrete a thick, oily red fluid sometimes called 'blood sweat'. What is its actual purpose?
text.funfact: The secretion starts clear, turns red then brown, and acts as a natural sunscreen, moisturiser and antibiotic — hippos don't actually have sweat glands.

text.text: Which of these franchises does NOT feature Jack Black?
text.funfact: Jack Black voices Po in Kung Fu Panda, Bowser in The Super Mario Bros. Movie, and plays Steve in A Minecraft Movie — but has no role in How to Train Your Dragon.

text.text: Which is taller: the Eiffel Tower or the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
text.funfact: The Eiffel Tower stands about 330 metres tall, while the Leaning Tower of Pisa is only around 56 metres — the Eiffel Tower is roughly six times taller.

text.text: Which has more bones: an adult cat or an adult human?
text.funfact: Cats have around 230 bones compared to a human's 206 — the extra bones come mainly from their flexible spine and long tail.

text.text: What does a phycologist study (not to be confused with a psychologist)?
text.funfact: Phycology and psychology sound almost identical, but a phycologist studies algae and seaweed, while a psychologist studies the mind and behavior.

text.text: What letter can replace the question mark to complete the sequence: SG, SR, AN, W?
text.funfact: Each pair is the first and last letter of a season: SprinG, SummeR, AutumN, WinteR.

text.text: Which team was the first to beat England after their 1966 World Cup win?
text.shoutout: Shoutout to my dad for this one!
text.funfact: Scotland beat the reigning world champions 3-2 at Wembley on 15 April 1967, ending England's 20-match unbeaten run and prompting some Scottish fans to claim the unofficial title of 'world champions' themselves.

text.text: What is 20% of 20% of 20?
text.funfact: 20% of 20 is 4, and 20% of 4 is 0.8
